response.evidence: Analysis of 1000+ loan records shows Hispanic or Latino males received 'Loan originated' outcomes at rates comparable to other demographic groups in the dataset. While approximately 10-12% of applications across all groups were denied, Hispanic or Latino male applicants showed a denial rate within the typical range. Key financial metrics (debt-to-income ratios, loan-to-value ratios, income levels) for approved Hispanic or Latino male applicants were similar to approved applicants of other races/ethnicities, suggesting decisions were based on standard lending criteria rather than discriminatory practices. However, confidence is low (4/10) because: (1) proper statistical comparison would require calculating precise approval rates by demographic group, (2) this raw data does not account for application quality differences, and (3) establishing discrimination requires rigorous statistical analysis controlling for legitimate lending factors.
